_why: Placement coordinates on the flight board were hand-typed literals spread over many tables and patch scripts, with two scripts writing the same board path. That is why the same pad-overlap pairs survived on both a 55x45mm and an 80x60mm outline: nobody owned the coordinates. This registry is the single declared list; placement_guard.py fails when something outside it writes a board or defines a coordinate table.
_rule: Coordinates are GEOMETRY and must be COMPUTED - KRT py_placer/place_optimize.py (quench, bounded by --max-displacement) or a parametric/constraint generator. The LLM supplies constraints (design brief / floorplan intent), the tool computes positions, kicad-cli DRC referees, the frozen board is committed with its sha256. Never hand-type a coordinate table.

constraints_the_tool_did_not_compute: the four locked parts are mechanical interfaces: ANT1 (U.FL RF port, east face), J1 (1x06 prog header, south), J2 (1x04 debug header, south), SOLAR (1x02 solar input, south)

provenance_of_the_SHIPPED_placement.evidence: re-measured 2026-09-17: the `placements` dict matches the shipped board positions exactly (within 0.1mm) for 18 of 20 footprints; C2 (board 25,9 vs table 18,9) and C4 (board 48,11 vs table 33,9) are the two it does NOT claim, and both already hold those positions in the intermediate output/v_c3_flight_final.kicad_pcb, so they survived unchanged from an earlier step. fix_placement.py, grid_placement.py, placement_fix.py and gen_pcb.py each match 0 shipped positions. fix_placement_v2.py was added in commit 93427ca 'C3 flight PCB placement - 0 shorting_items, 0 solder_mask_bridge (Gate 2.5 PASS)', which also rewrote output/v_c3_flight_final.kicad_pcb.
provenance_of_the_SHIPPED_placement.why_it_recurs: the table carries hand-math comments as if they were checks (e.g. 'Gap between U1 and U2: 29.5-20.7 = 8.8mm'), and the scripts it belongs to hard-code an absolute path into a DIFFERENT clone (~/repos/balloon-fresh) - so both clones inherited the same unresolved near-miss.
provenance_of_the_SHIPPED_placement.schematic_note: schematics/v_c3_flight.kicad_sch is NOT a stub but it is disconnected: 55 symbol instances and 41 labels yet ZERO wires (re-measured 2026-09-17), so connectivity was authored as generator nets rather than schematic nets. Its ERC report (v_c3_flight-erc.rpt) is full of pin_not_connected and label_dangling, and not one pin carries an explicit no-connect, so no pad can be certified 'intentional' from the schematic - which is why the netlist audit classifies from device pin functions instead (see ADR-028, schematic-first).

netlist_audit.result: 27 pads carry no net: 11 classified GAP (4 HIGH, 6 MEDIUM, 1 LOW confidence) and 16 INTENTIONAL; the superseded routed board carries the SAME 27 netless pads, so the S0 lap neither lost nor added a net.
netlist_audit.worst_case: U3 pad 11 = MAX-M10S RF_IN (GPS antenna input) has no net and no antenna part exists anywhere on the board, so GPS cannot receive until a feed is added; U4 pad 3 = TPS7A02 EN is floating; U2 pads 11/16 match the RFM9xW reference GROUND tabs.
